A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
adenocarcinoid meningioma is a rare variant of malignant meningiomas that is characterized by a glandular growth pattern with cytological features of adenocarcina.
adenocarcinomas and secretory meningiomas share a common embryological derivation, and that adenocarcionoma-like metaplsia is the result of malignant transformation of meningothelial cells.

The main takeaway from our work is that

, in the setting of a dural-based neoplasm with gland-like structures and a metastatic carcinoma-like appearance, a meningothelial component should be sought and, if identified, will help to establish the correct diagnosis of meningioma with epithelial metaplastic change.
, although meningiomas are known to undergo epithelial metaplastic changes, these changes are usually limited to the formation of secretory cells.
meningiomas can exhibit a wide range and combination of histologic and genetic features, and the pathologist must remain cognizant of this fact to avoid misdiagnoses.
